name: SPX, the opening lane's call: 10 minutes ahead, measured in tape units
how_to_use: Step 4 of the opening lane. The state is the lane's live answers from step 2, each rewritten by code as one sentence with how sure JEV was, plus a context line that states the tape unit in index points for this read (the middle of the last three 5-minute slice ranges, held at a fixed share of the day's expected move until 09:45, floored after; spx_jev/cuts.py).

One question rides on the sentences: where price is 10 minutes on, in five steps, so direction and size come from one answer. Code grades direction from the summed odds of the up and down steps and size from the summed odds of the big steps, against the bar 10 minutes after the read.

The bands are in tape units, filled from spx_jev/cuts.py, and the base rates are counted on SPX's opening reads with those bands (spec/cuts.json). The context line names the bands in points for the read, because JEV cannot turn a unit and a fraction into a price.
This is a forecast, graded by the bars, never a call. Its grades and tally live under state/spx_jev/lanes/tape/ and never touch the live lane.

next_10.ask: Where is price ten minutes from now, and how far?
next_10.why: The lane's one sum: direction and size in a single answer, sized by the tape.
next_10.instructions: Read `context.unit` for what one tape unit is in points right now and where the flat, small and big bands fall for this read, then `answers`, one sentence per question JEV has already answered about this moment, each ending with how sure it was. Taken together, where is price at the end of the next 10 minutes? Answer down_big, down_small, flat, up_small, up_big or unsure.

criteria.down_big: price ends more than {tape_big_units} of a tape unit below where it is now, the big band down; on this index's opening reads that happens about {tape_down_big_pct}% of the time
criteria.down_small: price ends below where it is now by more than {tape_flat_units} of a tape unit and no more than {tape_big_units} of a unit, the small band down; about {tape_down_small_pct}% of the time
criteria.flat: price ends within {tape_flat_units} of a tape unit of where it is now, either way; the common case, about {tape_flat_pct}% of the time
criteria.up_small: price ends above where it is now by more than {tape_flat_units} of a tape unit and no more than {tape_big_units} of a unit, the small band up; about {tape_up_small_pct}% of the time
criteria.up_big: price ends more than {tape_big_units} of a tape unit above where it is now, the big band up; about {tape_up_big_pct}% of the time
criteria.unsure: the answers pull hard both ways, so neither the common case nor any one step can be backed
